Is this by= spec natively lowerable end to end (Phase 7 J7, F24)?

Source: R/join.R
join_by_natively_supported.Rd

TRUE for everything join_by_is_non_equi() already called equi (no change there – J6 native hash-join path). For a genuinely non-equi join_by() object, native lowering additionally requires one of:

  • A plain non-equi join (every condition's filter is "none"): every operator is one this package's AST lowering understands (join_native_non_equi_ops). A non-equi condition comparing two STRING columns is native too (F24): lower_join() maps both sides onto INT32 codes of one shared order (apply_join_key_casts()), because cudf's AST evaluator can't compare strings. A STRING against anything else stays on the CPU fallback.

  • A rolling join (join_by_rolling_native(), F24): exactly one closest() condition plus == conditions. A missing/misspelled column name is NOT checked here – left to validate_join_cols()'s own proper error downstream on the native path (safer than silently routing an outright user typo to a fallback that would just re-raise the same error one layer later).

Usage

join_by_natively_supported(by, x, y)
